note: CI eval gates (spec §14; docs/eval-golden-set.md §6). EVERY number below is justified one by one in docs/eval/gate-model.md, which is the record, not this file. TWO layers, both ratchet UP only: `gates` are the aggregate floors, `per_language` the floors for every language the harness reports, so a weak language can no longer hide inside a healthy average (spec §14.3). A language the harness measures and this file does not name FAILS the gate check: an ungated language is the hole these floors close. Each floor is the HONEST CURRENT VALUE: the LOWEST value observed across NINE live runs of this exact prompt, corpus and model configuration on 2026-07-31 (eight local plus the first live gate on main, which is the one that showed the query-rewrite band is wider than eight identical local runs suggested), rounded down to two decimals of the TRUE fraction, never of the displayed percentage (54/73 prints as 74.0% and floors to 0.73, not 0.74). Never the specification target where the project sits below it, because a permanently red gate is not a gate, it teaches people to bypass it; and never inside a metric's run-to-run band, because a flaky gate gets ignored. No floor here was lowered: every aggregate floor is above the v1 value it replaces. Lowering one is a deliberate act that must be justified in the pull request that does it, with the measurement that justifies it.
chat_note: chat_gates: rule checks are all-must-pass in the harness; mean_coverage gates the MEAN of LLM-judged coverage across graded cases. Calibrated 2026-07-21 from the first temperature-0 baseline (mean 92.9% over 2 graded cases, atlas_scope 100 / who_is_ana 86): 0.65 leaves margin for residual provider nondeterminism on a small denominator while a broken prompt (historical degraded drill: single-digit coverage) lands far below. Ratchet UP only, same policy as gates.

vertical.note: The VERTICAL corpus's floors (V2.3 item 6.4): 44 labelled cases over 13 real public documents, reported and gated SEPARATELY from the core corpus above and NEVER averaged into it, because a hard new corpus folded into a mature one hides both signals. These floors are LOWER than the core ones and that is the expected, published result rather than a regression: real documents carry page furniture, registry metadata, tables flattened by a PDF text layer and a 1987 scan's OCR noise that no written fixture contains. THREE FLOORS ARE 0.00 (contradiction precision, contradiction recall, supersedes accuracy) and a floor of zero cannot fail: it is a published statement that the capability is absent on this corpus, with the denominator printed beside it, not a standard being met. Every number is justified in docs/eval/gate-model.md under the 2026-08-08 addendum, on the same terms as every other floor here: measured live, set below the worse of two runs by a margin sized from what one case is worth on that denominator, ratchet UP only, never a target the project sits below. `xl` is the cross-language pair set (English against Croatian on one act); it is a measured set like a language and it is gated like one, and its three extraction floors sit at 1.00 to assert it stays reconciliation-only. `rewrite_accuracy` is absent on purpose: the query-rewrite suite is a corpus of chat turns, not of documents, and gating a metric this corpus cannot measure would gate the harness's empty-arm convention rather than the system.
